summary: Mikel Burley specializes in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Essex under J. M. Bernstein and earned his PhD at the University of Bristol under John Peacock, later becoming Associate Professor at the University of Leeds.

Mikhail Izrailevich Tubyansky worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Theodore Stcherbatsky and Boris Vladimirtsov, later serving as naučnyj sotrudnik at the Asiatic Museum and teaching Bengali at the Leningrad Institute of Living Oriental Languages.

Mikhail Kudryavtsev was an Indologist who studied at Leningrad Topographical Technical School and Saint Petersburg State University. From 1948, he worked at the Institute of Ethnography, where he became staršij naučnyj sotrudnik in 1969.

Mikhail Nikolayevich Peterson was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Moscow State University under Wiktor Jan Porzeziński, Filipp Fedorovich Fortunatov, and Nikolai Trubetzkoy, and later served as a Docent there from 1916 to 1952.
Mikhail Pokrovsky was a scholar who studied under Vsevolod Miller and Filipp Fedorovich Fortunatov.

Mikhail Sergeevich Troitsky worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts of the Russian Academy of Sciences under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy and later held a post at the University of Chicago.
Mikhaïl Peterson studied under Wiktor Jan Porzeziński and Filipp Fedorovich Fortunatov, and he taught Pavel Grintser and Vyacheslav Ivanov.
Mikio Otsuki specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. As attested in 2007, he served as a professor at Hanazono University and a research fellow at Manpuku-ji.

Mikisaburo Mori was a scholar of philosophy and sinology who studied at Kyoto University and Osaka University. He held professorships at Osaka High School, Osaka University (1966–1973), and Bukkyo University (around 1973–1982).

Mikołaj Kruszewski was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Warsaw and under Jan Niecisław Baudouin de Courtenay at Kazan State University, where he held the chair of Sanskrit and Comparative Grammar of Indo-European Languages.

Mikołaj Rudnicki was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied under Jan Michał Rozwadowski at Jagiellonian University and served as Professor of Indo-European Linguistics at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań from 1919 to 1950.

Mildred Archer was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She earned an M.A. and D.Litt. from St Hilda's College, Oxford, and served as Keeper of Prints and Drawings at the India Office from 1954 to 1980.

Milena Hübschmannová worked in Indology and linguistics. After earning her PhD from Charles University, she held posts at the Oriental Institute and Czechoslovak Academy of Sciences, returning to Charles University in 1991 as Professor of Romani.

Miles Bronson was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Colgate University and Colgate Rochester Crozer Divinity School from around 1834 to 1836. In 1837, he founded the American Baptist Missionary Union.

Milman Parry was a scholar of linguistics who studied at the University of California, Berkeley, and under Antoine Meillet at the University of Paris. He held an academic post at Harvard University from around 1929 to 1935.

Milo Cleveland Beach is a historian and Indologist educated at Harvard. He held posts at the Fogg Art Museum, Williams College, the Smithsonian Institution, and served as Director of the National Museum of Asian Art.
Miloslav Krása was an Indologist and historian who studied at Charles University under Vincenc Pořízka and at the University of Allahabad. He taught at Charles University from 1954 to 1997.

Miloš Borecký worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology, earning a PhD at Charles University under Vincenc Lesný. He served as a librarian at the National Library of the Czech Republic and worked at the Library of Congress.

Milton Singer was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his PhD under Rudolf Carnap at the University of Chicago. He taught there from 1941, serving as Professor of Anthropology between 1954 and 1979.

Min Lin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who was a postgraduate student at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, with an attested post as a Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
